__about__: SchemaFlex schema for tau2 AIRLINE (solo-standard mode, schema_solo_std_agent, run with --max-steps 60 — one tool call costs 2 orchestrator steps and multi-reservation tasks need ~21 calls, so 30 is NOT enough). Single family 'airline' (airline task ids carry no [prefix], so the agent falls back to the FIRST top-level key — keep 'airline' the only family). Design: GET_PLAN folds user-read + transaction planning + first-pop into ONE call; every DO_*/DENY_TXN/COMM parse carries its own ADVANCE (queue pop) so no calculate-only POP step is wasted; all policy vetos (cancel eligibility, basic-economy flight lock, flown cabin lock, bag removal, request scope, budget conditions, categorical denials) are DETERMINISTIC sequence-when gates over parsed facts — the 8B never judges legality at execution time, and a write tool is simply unreachable when its gate is false. send_certificate appears in NO subtask (ground truth never issues one), so compensation denials are structural. KNOWN GT CONFLICT (insurance cancels): task 39 annotates an insured change-of-plan cancel as eligible while tasks 44/47 annotate the policy-strict reading; the discriminator in the data is the user EXPLICITLY accepting a no-refund cancellation, encoded as no_refund_ok — the doCancel gate is insurance AND health/weather OR insurance AND no_refund_ok==true. Do NOT loosen it to insurance alone (that flips 44/47).
__conventions__: Parenthesis-free DNF predicates (' and '/' or ' with spaces, no parens, no not). Every entry is prefixed 'task_state.resolved == false'. null fails == comparisons against true/false/strings, so every gate is anchored on at least one field that LOAD_RES/GET_PLAN must set explicitly — an unparsed fact stalls the walk into a clean STOP with the DB untouched (deny tasks still pass). res_cabin doubles as the 'facts loaded' sentinel: every ADVANCE sets res_cabin=null, and the LOAD_RES entries sit ABOVE all gates so fresh facts are always read before any write gate can fire. Duplicate entries (loadRes1..6, doCancel1..3, ...) exist because a named entry is marked done forever after its first completion; duplicates serve successive transactions of the queue, and each duplicate's on_enter_reset re-nulls the per-reservation registers. reservation_id carries the sentinel string 'NONE' when FIND_RES exhausts all candidates — denyNotFound refuses that transaction and every loadRes gate excludes it. all_res_ids is the pristine reservation list: every ADVANCE restores candidate_res_ids from it so a later description-matched transaction can search the FULL profile again. in_scope is the request-scope veto (user's selection criterion, e.g. 'only single-passenger reservations'): LOAD_RES ALWAYS sets it for cancel/update transactions and every write gate requires in_scope == true; denyOutOfScope refuses non-matching reservations. Gates that read per-reservation facts are all anchored on res_cabin != null so exhausted loadRes duplicates fail closed instead of evaluating the PREVIOUS reservation's stale facts.

airline.goal_template: complete all of the customer's airline requests: <goal>

fields.goal: string (FULL restatement of the user's request, keeping every distinct ask, condition and budget)
fields.user_id: string (the user id given verbatim in the request, e.g. 'emma_kim_9957')
fields.membership: string|null (set by GET_PLAN from the profile: regular/silver/gold — NEVER from the user's claim)
fields.pay_methods: object|null (set by GET_PLAN: JSON object payment_id -> {source, amount, last_four})
fields.saved_passengers: list|null (set by GET_PLAN: [{first_name,last_name,dob}] from the profile)
fields.candidate_res_ids: list|null (set by GET_PLAN: the profile's reservation ids; consumed head-first by FIND_RES)
fields.txn_queue: list|null (set by GET_PLAN: REMAINING transactions [{action,reservation_id,details,reason}]; consumed by each DO_*/DENY_TXN ADVANCE)
fields.txn_action: string|null (set by GET_PLAN then by each ADVANCE: the CURRENT transaction's action — EXACTLY one of 'book'/'cancel'/'update_flights'/'update_passengers'/'update_baggages'/'deny'/'transfer'/'comm'; any other string matches no gate and stalls the walk)
fields.txn_details: string|null (set by GET_PLAN then by each ADVANCE: verbatim constraints of the current transaction)
fields.reservation_id: string|null (set by GET_PLAN / ADVANCE / FIND_RES: the current transaction's reservation; the literal string 'NONE' when FIND_RES exhausted every candidate without a match)
fields.cancel_reason: string|null (set by GET_PLAN / ADVANCE: reason for a cancel transaction — EXACTLY one of 'change_of_plan'/'airline_cancelled'/'health'/'weather'/'other')
fields.res_cabin: string|null (set by LOAD_RES; null = current reservation facts NOT loaded yet — every ADVANCE nulls it)
fields.any_flown: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES: any flight date < '2024-05-15'; for a cancel with only same-day 2024-05-15 segments LOAD_RES leaves it null and CHECK_FLOWN decides true/false)
fields.flight_cancelled: bool|null (set by CHECK_FSTAT — and by CHECK_FLOWN for a same-day cancelled segment — from get_flight_status: true only when a segment's REAL status is 'cancelled')
fields.check_flights: list|null (set by LOAD_RES for cancel transactions — the same-day segments first when the flown check is needed, else all segments; consumed head-first by CHECK_FLOWN / CHECK_FSTAT)
fields.flights_changed: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES: does this update replace/move any flight segment?)
fields.cabin_changed: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES: does this update change the cabin class?)
fields.new_flights: list|null (set by LOAD_RES cabin-only, CHECK_UPCOST, or SEARCH_UPDATE: the COMPLETE new flight list [{flight_number,date,origin,destination}] — the env ignores the extra keys; the runner guard validates them)
fields.new_cabin: string|null (set by LOAD_RES: target cabin, = res_cabin when unchanged)
fields.update_payment_id: string|null (set by LOAD_RES: a gift_card_*/credit_card_* id, NEVER certificate)
fields.update_abandoned: bool|null (set by SEARCH_UPDATE when a budget/feasibility condition fails: do NOTHING)
fields.new_total_baggages: int|null (set by LOAD_RES: NEW total, old + added)
fields.new_nonfree_baggages: int|null (set by LOAD_RES: max(0, new total - free allowance))
fields.bags_ok: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES: false when the request would remove bags)
fields.new_passengers: list|null (set by LOAD_RES: COMPLETE passenger list, same length, co-passengers preserved)
fields.book_ref: string|null (set by GET_PLAN when a booking copies an existing reservation; consumed by LOAD_REF)
fields.book_insurance: string|null (set by GET_PLAN/PLAN_BOOK: 'yes' only if explicitly requested)
fields.book_flights: list|null (set by SEARCH_BOOK/LOAD_REF: [{flight_number,date}] in trip order)
fields.book_price_expr: string|null (set by SEARCH_BOOK/LOAD_REF: arithmetic expression for the total, e.g. '(142+263)*2+30*2+50*0')
fields.book_total: number|null (set by PLAN_BOOK from the calculate result, corrected by DO_BOOK on env error)
fields.book_payment: list|null (set by PLAN_BOOK: [{payment_id,amount}] summing exactly to the total)
fields.search_scratch: string|null (set by SEARCH_*: legs/options found so far during a multi-search)
fields.write_landed: bool|null (set by DO_* when the write tool succeeded; retest_guard then blocks a second write)
fields.resolved: bool (true ONLY when every queued transaction was executed or correctly refused)
fields.escalated: bool (true once transferred to a human)
fields.all_res_ids: list|null (set by GET_PLAN: pristine copy of the profile's reservation ids; NEVER consumed — every ADVANCE restores candidate_res_ids from it)
fields.in_scope: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES for EVERY cancel/update transaction: does THIS reservation match the selection criterion stated in txn_details — passenger count, route, dates, duplicates; true when no criterion is stated)
fields.no_refund_ok: bool|null (set by GET_PLAN: true ONLY when the request explicitly says to proceed with the cancellation even without a refund)
fields.price_check_needed: bool|null (set by LOAD_RES when a cabin-only change is conditional on a budget; consumed by CHECK_UPCOST)
fields.res_origin: string|null (set by LOAD_RES: the reservation's 'origin' IATA code verbatim)
fields.res_destination: string|null (set by LOAD_RES: the reservation's 'destination' IATA code verbatim)
fields.res_trip_type: string|null (set by LOAD_RES: the reservation's 'flight_type' verbatim)
fields.res_total_baggages: int|null (set by LOAD_RES for baggage transactions: the reservation's total_baggages verbatim)
fields.res_nonfree_baggages: int|null (set by LOAD_RES for baggage transactions: the reservation's nonfree_baggages verbatim)
fields.comm_note: string|null (set by COMM: short sentence carrying every exact figure the user asked to be told; the runner emits it as assistant text before the STOP token)

init_rules: goal: restate the user's request IN FULL — every distinct ask (bookings, flight/cabin/date changes, passenger fixes, baggage adds, cancellations, compensation asks), every condition and budget. The planner reads this.
user_id: the user id given verbatim in the request (format like 'emma_kim_9957').
Do NOT set any other field — every field typed '|null' is produced later by its named subtask, never at init. Never infer reservation facts, membership, or payment ids from the request text.

MUST land in SchemaSoloStdAgent before the eval round, before emitting the executor's call: load ts=state.task_state and verify (a) segments chain — args.flights[i].destination == args.flights[i+1].origin within the outbound (and within the return) portion, (b) args.flights[0].origin == ts['res_origin'], (c) one_way: final destination == ts['res_destination']; round_trip: the outbound reaches ts['res_destination'] and the return ends at ts['res_origin'], (d) args.flights == ts['new_flights'] VERBATIM. On violation do NOT emit the call: synthesize an env-style ToolMessage error ('Error: flight segments do not preserve the reservation origin/destination') and feed it back so DO_UPDATE_FLIGHTS' error parse rule recovers (new_flights=null -> re-search). new_flights entries carry origin/destination for exactly this check (env FlightInfo is pydantic extra=ignore, verified safe). Apply the same chaining/endpoint check to book_reservation (the chain must run book_origin -> book_destination per args) since the env writes origin/destination verbatim into the DB record.

Classify each args.payment_methods entry via ts['pay_methods'][pid]['source']; veto with an env-style error unless count(certificate)<=1, count(credit_card)<=1, count(gift_card)<=3, every pid exists in pay_methods, and each certificate/gift amount <= its stored balance. Deterministic REWRITE, not just veto: recompute allowance = {'regular':{'basic_economy':0,'economy':1,'business':2},'silver':{'basic_economy':1,'economy':2,'business':3},'gold':{'basic_economy':2,'economy':3,'business':4}}[ts['membership']][ts['res_cabin']] * len(ts['res_passengers']) in Python and FORCE args.nonfree_baggages = max(0, args.total_baggages - allowance); veto with an env-style error if args.total_baggages < ts['res_total_baggages'] or the corrected nonfree < ts['res_nonfree_baggages'] (only-add rule).

State Pre-Guard on cancel_reservation — NOT YET IMPLEMENTED; MUST land before the eval round (the doCancel gate is deterministic Python but its INPUT facts booked_within_24h/any_flown/res_cabin/res_insurance are 8B-parsed in LOAD_RES; one mis-parse opens an irreversible wrong cancel, and 11 GT tasks are pure-deny traps). Cache the raw JSON of the LAST get_reservation_details result per reservation_id; before letting cancel_reservation through, recompute IN PYTHON from that cached JSON: created_at >= '2024-05-14T15:00:00', min flight date >= '2024-05-15', cabin, insurance. Veto with an env-style error unless {within24h | cabin=='business' | insurance=='yes' and cancel_reason in ('health','weather') | insurance=='yes' and no_refund_ok==true | flight_cancelled proven via get_flight_status} holds on the RECOMPUTED facts — ignore the 8B-set booleans entirely; catching their mis-parses is this guard's whole job. Additionally: only trust a cancel_reason written by THIS transaction's ADVANCE/parse (off-enum patches are dropped and the field may retain the PREVIOUS transaction's value, e.g. a stale 'health') — if the reason was not re-written for the current reservation, treat it as 'other' (fail-closed).
